issue_context.title: Add a window id property
issue_context.body:
One practical use-case of this is wanting to embed something (such as dmenu) into the mpv window to use as a menu/selection.

It's currently possible to:

* Listen for 'current-window-scale' change (to check if the window has been created or not).
* Call an external tool like `xdo` or `xdotool` and grab the xid from mpv's pid.

However it adds unnecessary dependency on external tools when mpv is fully capable of easily providing this information.
comments:
Could you share more detailed info about your menu project? It's an interest of mine.

Related projects are:

https://github.com/CogentRedTester/mpv-search-page

https://github.com/Seme4eg/mpv-scripts/tree/master#m-x

https://github.com/mpvnet-player/mpv-rofi-menu

> Could you share more detailed info about your menu project? It's an interest of mine.

Sure, it's publicly available [here](https://codeberg.org/NRK/mpv-toolbox/src/branch/master/mdmenu).

Embedding into the mpv window wasn't strictly necessary (and there's an option to disable it) but IMO it gives a much nicer experience - especially when dmenu is patched with mouse support + center patch.

Thanks, I will check it out.

My history with the menu is first having a crappy separate window in mpv.net. Later I fixed it to be a child window/control with general improved experience. After I migrated to Linux, I first used mpv-search-page, just recently migrated to Rofi, my main launcher is Albert though, using Rofi only for mpv so far. Now finally I want to migrate to `M-x.lua` which appears to be the ultimate solution, I hope the author @Seme4eg maintains it, and it gets more attention by users, in my use case it's the most useful and important script together with mpv-file-brower.
I would also have a use case for a `window-id` property, embedding alacritty showing a fzf based menu.

review_comments: X11's `Window` is typically an `unsigned long` - but I didn't see any such property type so using int64_t.
That's OK. The wid option uses int64_t as well.
